timeline.title: A Short History of a Well Earned Rest
items: Emperor Augustus set up a fund to reward soldiers who had finished their years of service.
Germany created one of the first national old age pensions, an idea the world soon followed.
In Britain, people over 70 collected their first state pension from the post office.
The United States passed the Social Security Act, so a lifetime of work led to a safer rest.
today: After {years} years, a new chapter begins. Easily the best one yet.

letters.title: Wise Words for the Next Chapter
items: Come, my friends, 'Tis not too late to seek a newer world.
How we spend our days is, of course, how we spend our lives.
Well done is better than well said.
The best time to plant a tree was twenty years ago. The next best is now.
letters.hand: They all say it beautifully. We just say: thank you, {who}.

facts.title: The Science of a Happy Retirement
items: Time spent in gardens and green spaces is linked to lower stress and a brighter mood.
The brain keeps building new connections all through life. New hobbies keep it sharp.
Many studies find people tend to feel more content from their fifties onwards.
Strong friendships are linked to longer, healthier lives. Lunch dates are basically medicine.
Body clocks shift with age, so many of us wake earlier. The lie in may start at six.
Some bristlecone pine trees are over 4,000 years old. Still standing, still growing.
facts.hand: Science can explain a lot. It still cannot explain how {who} made it all look so easy.

world.title: Why the World Is Better With You in It
world.lead: Because of you, the world got:
items: {years} years of hard work and good humour.
Advice that was always worth listening to.
A kettle that was never left empty.
Stories we will be telling for years.
Patience, even on the busiest days.
A friend to everyone who walked in.
And a legend we will never replace.
world.close: The world is better because of you, {who}. Ours most of all.

promises.title: Our promises to you
items: To keep telling your famous stories.
To visit, and bring the good biscuits.
To never call you about work. Probably.
To pass on everything you taught us.
To miss you, always, and say so often.

note.title: What we believe a legend is
paras: We make magazines for a living, but some feel different. This was one of them.
We believe a career is not only the job title. It is the people you helped, the problems you quietly fixed, the kindness that made ordinary days better.
{who}, someone wanted you to have something special. Not a card anyone could buy, but pages full of you: your face, your stories, the years that made you a legend.
That someone is {from}. And from everything they told us, you will be missed more than you know.
